summary: Roger T. Ames is a philosopher and sinologist who studied at the University of British Columbia, National Taiwan University, and SOAS University of London under D. C. Lau. He served as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi from circa 1978 to 2016.

Roland Barthes worked in philosophy and linguistics, studying at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, Lycée Montaigne, the Faculty of Arts of Paris, and under Émile Benveniste. He held posts at CNRS (circa 1952–1959), EHESS (circa 1962–1976), and the Collège de France (1976–1980).
Roland Ferenczi is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. In 2026, he was attested as a visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University and as a project employee at the University of Hamburg.
Roland Steiner is a scholar in Indology and Tibetology who studied under Michael Hahn. In 2002, he was attested as an assistant professor at the University of Marburg.

Historian Roland Wenzlhuemer earned his doctorate at the University of Salzburg and completed his habilitation at Heidelberg University. He held positions at Humboldt University, ZMO, Heidelberg University (starting in 2008; professor in 2014), Basel (2013–2014), and Munich (professor in 2017).

Rolf Alfred Stein was a scholar in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied under teachers including Granet, Maspero, and Demiéville. He held posts at INALCO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1951–1975), and the Collège de France (1965–1982).
Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Helmut Tauscher.

Romila Thapar is a historian and Indologist who earned her doctorate at SOAS University of London under A. L. Basham. She was a professor at the University of Delhi (1963–1970) and held a chair at Jawaharlal Nehru University (1970–1991, 1993).
Ron Garry is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

Ronald D. Schwartz is a scholar in Tibetology. He held a post as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland (attested 1998) and served as an Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

Ronald E. Purser works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Koshin Ogui in 1985 and held posts at Loyola University Chicago (circa 1989–1997) and San Francisco State University (beginning circa 1997).

Ronald Egan is a Sinologist who earned his PhD at Harvard University. He held academic posts at Harvard (circa 1978–1983), the University of California, Santa Barbara (circa 1993–2012), and Stanford University (circa 2012).

Ronald Eric Emmerick specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under Harold Walter Bailey and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1971 to 2001.

Ronald Inden is an Indologist and historian who has held appointments at the University of Chicago, where he is attested as Professor Emeritus of History and South Asian Languages and Civilizations in 2026.

Ronald M. Davidson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 1985 and was attested as a faculty member at Fairfield University between 2002 and 2005.
Ronald M. Kaplan is a scholar in linguistics and computational linguistics who held posts at the University of Texas at Austin and the Palo Alto Research Center.

Ronald Neufeldt is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held posts at the University of Calgary from circa 1977 until 2007, serving as an associate professor from circa 1981 to 1990 and later becoming professor emeritus.

Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1980. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1991) and the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).
Rong Geng was a scholar in archaeology, Sinology, and linguistics. He studied at Peking University from circa 1922 to 1926 and held an academic post at Yenching University from circa 1926 to 1941.
